title: Bounded rewind to the input start
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $r,s$ be states and $d$ an optional state. Suppose that from state $r$, for every input symbol and tuple of work-tape symbols, the machine moves the input head left and enters $s$. From state $s$, it moves left and stays in $s$ whenever an input symbol is scanned, and moves right and enters $d$ whenever a blank is scanned; these transitions make no writes, do not move any work-tape head, and emit no output. For every configuration $c$ on input $x$ whose state is $r$, there is a number of steps $t\le p+2$, where $p$ is the input-head position of $c$, after which the machine is in the configuration obtained from $c$ by changing only its state to $d$ and its input-head position to $1$.

replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean
alphabet on input $x$, with a start state $r$, a scanning state $s$, and an
optional dispatch state $d$, such that regardless of the symbols read: from $r$
the machine always moves the input head left (clamped at the left boundary
blank) and enters $s$; from $s$ it moves left and stays in $s$ when an input
symbol is scanned, and moves right and passes to $d$ when a blank is scanned;
and none of these transitions touches a work tape, a work head, or the output.
Let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ in state $r$ whose input head is at position
$p \in \{0,\dots,\abs{x}+1\}$, where position $0$ is the left boundary blank.
Then there exists $t \le p + 2$ such that running $M$ for $t$ steps from $c$
yields the configuration that agrees with $c$ in every component except that
its state is $d$ and its input head is at position $1$.
